name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with schistosomiasis

ethnicAssociations: Populations in endemic regions of Africa, South America, and the Middle East

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Right heart catheterization criteria for pulmonary arterial hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary artery wedge pressure (PAWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Evidence of schistosomal infection or exposure (serology, stool/urine microscopy, or history of residence in endemic area)
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as connective tissue disease, congenital heart disease, or chronic thromboembolic disease
Echocardiographic findings suggestive of elevated pulmonary artery pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure ≥ 25 mmHg with PAWP ≤ 15 mmHg by right heart catheterization plus evidence of schistosomal infection and exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires invasive hemodynamic confirmation and epidemiological or laboratory evidence of schistosomiasis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Exertional dyspnea due to elevated pulmonary arterial pressure
searchTerms: dyspnea due to high lung pressure

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive fatigue related to right ventricular dysfunction
searchTerms: progressive fatigue from right heart issues

pathognomonic.symptomName: Signs of right heart failure including peripheral edema and jugular venous distension
searchTerms: swelling in legs and neck veins
leg swelling and bulging neck veins

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort or angina-like chest pain
Syncope or near-syncope episodes on exertion
searchTerms: fainting or near fainting during exercise

common.symptomName: Palpitations due to arrhythmias secondary to right heart strain
searchTerms: irregular heartbeat from right heart strain
palpitations due to heart rhythm problems

occasional.symptomName: Hemoptysis due to pulmonary artery rupture or infarction
searchTerms: coughing up blood from lung vessel damage
blood in sputum due to lung artery injury

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal distension from hepatomegaly and ascites
searchTerms: belly swelling from enlarged liver and fluid
abdominal bloating from liver and fluid buildup
stomach enlargement due to liver and ascites
cyanosis due to poor oxygen levels

rare.symptomName: Ascites secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from heart failure
ascites caused by right heart failure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP levels
imaging: Chest X-ray showing enlarged pulmonary arteries and right ventricular enlargement
Echocardiography demonstrating elevated pulmonary artery pressures and right ventricular hypertrophy
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure
other: Detection of schistosome eggs in stool or urine samples
History of exposure to endemic freshwater bodies

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of schistosomal infection or exposure
Often younger patients with no endemic exposure
History of pulmonary embolism or thrombosis
Different treatment approach including possible surgical intervention

redFlags: Rapid progression of exertional dyspnea and syncope
Signs of right heart failure such as peripheral edema and jugular venous distension
Hemoptysis indicating possible pulmonary artery rupture
references: Simonneau G, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Santos M, et al. Schistosomiasis-associated pulmonary arterial hypertension: a systematic review. Eur Respir Rev. 2021.
